_comment: Issue #651 — mutation testing scoped to a curated set of pure, high-value core modules that have focused unit tests. Run via `npm run test:mutation`; nightly/manual in CI only (mutation runs are slow). Issue #751 added the security-critical injection-guard detector to the scope, ratcheting `break` 45 -> 50. Issue #896 added secret-scanner and strengthened redaction tests, ratcheting `break` 50 -> 64. Baseline re-measured 2026-09-10 (~41m, concurrency 2): combined 68.97% — chunk-id 54.94%, hybrid-retrieval 93.15%, lexical-bm25 50.00%, redaction 69.95%, secret-scanner 80.84%, injection-guard 69.72%. Issue #903 added the two fail-closed security-decision modules sensitivity-policy and kb-write-policy with focused invariant tests. Scoped mutation run of just those two files (2026-09-16, ~3m, concurrency 2) scored 93.77% combined — sensitivity-policy 95.26%, kb-write-policy 90.36% — with every fail-closed decision-value mutant killed (remaining survivors are equivalent mutants where the fail-closed fallback converges with the recognized-value branch, plus benign error-message string literals). Both files raise the combined score, so `break` stays at 64 (a safe non-flaky floor); the nightly full run supplies the authoritative combined for the next ratchet. Issue #1028 added relevance-judge.ts — the keep/drop fail-safe that can silently delete retrieved results and downgrades hallucinated 'drop' verdicts to 'keep' — to the scope, with a comprehensive deterministic suite (relevance-judge.test.ts, added to jest.stryker.config.cjs testMatch) covering both the JSON-salvage/downgrade parser and the previously-uncovered LLM-orchestration path (policy gate, deterministic shuffle, prompt assembly, outbound redaction dispatch, prompt hashing). The suite also hardened parseJudgeJson to reject well-formed-but-non-object judge JSON (null/array/scalar) with RelevanceJudgeError instead of letting a raw TypeError escape the fail-safe contract. A scoped mutation run of just relevance-judge.ts (2026-11-03, ~30s, concurrency 2) scored 91.42% (277/303 killed); the remaining survivors are equivalent mutants — markdown-fence regex variants the JSON-repair fallback masks, the defensive 'unknown' source branch the policy gate makes unreachable, whitespace-trim no-ops around the tolerant JSON.parse, the 'utf-8' default-encoding literal, and the empty-override guard that converges with the provider-remote fallback. relevance-judge sits well above the combined baseline, so `break` stays at 64 (a safe non-flaky floor); the nightly full run supplies the authoritative combined for the next ratchet. Only the deterministic unit tests are in the Stryker `testMatch` (jest.stryker.config.cjs); the fast-check property suites are deliberately excluded so the gate stays deterministic — their random seeds would jitter the mutant verdicts. `thresholds.break` sits a few points under the combined baseline so the gate catches regressions without flaking on run-to-run jitter; ratchet it upward as the suite improves.
